text:
dana: Heads-up — seeing a steady tail latency increase in eu-west-1 GPU hosts since ~03:20 UTC. p95 token latency up ~2.4x and slab allocator commit spikes aligned to one tenant's allocations. Possible slab hog from long-lived model sessions. :rotating_light:
alejandro: ugh. do we have tenant id or host IDs yet?
sam: infra-bot posted a flow: alert -> host list -> top allocs. paste logs?
dana: infra-bot already, but quick top hosts: gpu-14, gpu-15, gpu-18. Tenant=team-x-prod (suspected). I can share flame graph later.
infra-bot: [ALERT] slab_hog_detector: eu-west-1 cluster: slab_hog_score=12.7, affected_hosts=[gpu-14,gpu-15,gpu-18], window=5m.
maria: if it's team-x-prod, they're on shared slices, right? moving to dedicated would avoid this but cost impact is nontrivial. what's the failure mode — cache thrash or kernel slab leak?
dana: early signal looks like aggressive pinned allocations + short free patterns causing slab churn and increased PCIe stalls. not a leak, more of a hog under churn.
sam: actionable: add a quick detection + soft-quarantine rule: if slab_hog_score > 8 for 3m then mark tenant hot and route new allocs to reserved warm-pool or preemptively throttle. also surface to SRE for manual follow-up.
leo: can we do that without causing immediate OOMs for them? want graceful fallback (reduce concurrency, not hard kill).
dana: agreed — propose soft quota: reduce concurrency by 30% and move new requests to preemptible dedicated lane. fallback to full after 10m of healthy metrics.
alejandro: need a PromQL to detect. rough: `sum by (tenant) (rate(slab_alloc_count[5m])) / sum by (tenant) (slab_active_bytes) > 0.1` — naive but a start.
sam: nice. throw in KV cache miss rate correlation: `increase(kv_cache_evictions{tenant="$TENANT"}[5m]) > 100` then we escalate.
maria: ops question — if we move tenant to dedicated warm-pool, will that blow our reserved capacity budgets? we have 2 warm-slices in eu-west pinned for enterprise.
leo: might be ok for short term if we auto-evict after 10m. long-term we should talk with team-x about dedicated reservations + cost share.
dana: i'll run a quick canary: implement detection rule on staging metrics and a playbook: 1) detect 2) soft-throttle 3) move new allocs to warm-pool 4) notify tenant and @oncall 5) escalate to dedicate if repeated 3x/day.
oncall-bot: @oncall paging: potential noisy-tenant detected for team-x-prod in eu-west-1. Runbook link: https://internal.runbook/slab-hog-response
sam: small config prototype (k8s pseudo):
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: QuotaRule
metadata:
  name: slab-hog-soft-quota
spec:
  trigger:
    metric: slab_hog_score
    threshold: 8
    window: 3m
  action:
    type: soft_throttle
    reduce_concurrency_pct: 30
    route: warm-pool-preemptible
    revert_after: 10m
```
alejandro: can you post the flamegraph after you run the probe? i'll correlate NIC/Pcie counters.
dana: will do. i'll also add a telemetry tag so we can backfill how often this happens per tenant.
maria: tagging for finance — cc @finance if we hit >2 warm-pool moves for a tenant per week we bill or open a cost review.
leo: +1. the detection rule should include a cooldown per tenant (e.g., 1h) to avoid flip-flopping.
dana: noted. will roll detection to eu-west staging then prod if green. keeping everyone updated in this thread. :thumbsup:
